title: Futuro perfecto: conjeturas sobre lo ya ocurrido

sections.content: The future perfect (habrán alcanzado, se habrá construido) has a second job besides predicting what will be finished by some future point: it also expresses a confident guess about something already completed, when exact evidence is missing -- "they will have reached..." meaning "they probably reached..." This is exactly the tool a historian reaches for when the records are incomplete. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Dado el número de misiones organizadas, estas seguramente habrán alcanzado, hacia finales de la década de 1920, a una parte considerable de la población rural.
items.english: Given the number of missions organized, these will surely have reached, by the late 1920s, a considerable portion of the rural population.

items.spanish: Para entonces se habrá construido, solo en México, un número de escuelas rurales varias veces superior al que existía antes de la revolución.
items.english: By then, in Mexico alone, a number of rural schools several times greater than existed before the revolution will have been built.

items.spanish: Quienes hayan revisado su impacto real habrán confirmado que la educación pública resultó decisiva para construir un sentido de pertenencia nacional.
items.english: Those who have reviewed its real impact will have confirmed that public education proved decisive in building a sense of national belonging.

items.spanish: La escuela, el maestro y el idioma nacional se habrán convertido, en la práctica, en la cara más visible del propio Estado.
items.english: The school, the teacher, and the national language will have become, in practice, the most visible face of the state itself.

sections.content: Seguramente habrán alcanzado and probablemente habrán confirmado both pair the future perfect with an adverb of probability -- a natural combination in Spanish when you're reasoning your way to a likely conclusion rather than citing a hard number.
